Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

although conjunction

also though, even though, albeit, while (conceding)

classical

Cic. Sen. 44: quamquam immoderātīs epulīs caret senectūs, modicīs tamen convīviīs dēlectārī potest

quamquam

conjunction, with the indicative

Grants a fact; the main clause often has tamen. At the head of a sentence it also corrects what was just said: “and yet”.

Other words

  • quamvīs — although, however much

    conjunction, with the subjunctive in classical prose; with an adjective or adverb, “however” · also used · classical · Ov. Met. 6.376: quamvīs sint sub aquā, sub aquā maledīcere temptant; Cic. Tusc. 2.13: ager quamvīs fertilis

    “As much as you like”: grants a supposition, or a fact put as one. With an adjective it needs no verb: quamvīs fertilis, however fertile.

  • etsī (tametsī) — although, even though

    conjunction, with the indicative for a fact · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.53.1: ego etsī nihil habeō quod ad tē scrībam, scrībō tamen; Ter. And. 348: Obtundis, tametsī intellegō.

    Built on sī: “even if”, used of a fact. Often answered by tamen.

  • cum (+ subjunctive) — although, while

    conjunction, with the subjunctive · also used · classical · Ov. Pont. 1.3.39–40: cum bene sit clausae caveā Pandīone nātae, nītitur in silvās illa redīre suās

    Concessive cum: the fact that might have stopped the main clause; often with tamen.

Examples

  • quamquam immoderātīs epulīs caret senectūs, modicīs tamen convīviīs dēlectārī potest

    although old age goes without lavish feasts, it can still enjoy modest dinnersCic. Sen. 44

  • quamquam suus cuique dignus est

    though every parent’s own child is worthy of itQuint. 1.1.24

  • quamvīs sint sub aquā, sub aquā maledīcere temptant

    though they are under water, under water they try to curseOv. Met. 6.376

  • ego etsī nihil habeō quod ad tē scrībam, scrībō tamen quia tēcum loquī videor

    though I have nothing to write to you, I write all the same, because I seem to be talking with youCic. Att. 12.53.1

  • Obtundis, tametsī intellegō.

    You keep going on, though I understand.Ter. And. 348

  • cum bene sit clausae caveā Pandīone nātae, nītitur in silvās illa redīre suās

    though Pandion’s daughter is well off shut in her cage, she strains to go back to her woodsOv. Pont. 1.3.39–40

See also even if, however.
